fields.Base style · legacy numeric ranges: A reference family for the beer. Automatic matching compares your ABV, IBU and SRM targets, plus optional gravity ranges, with the catalog’s older numeric ranges. It cannot identify flavor, ingredients or fermentation process from numbers alone. Manual selection locks that style until automatic matching is resumed. It preserves your numeric targets, flavor sliders and ingredient choices; only suggestions and the reference ranges update.
fields.Automatic style matching: When enabled, edits to ABV, IBU, color or optional gravity limits update the closest numeric style and ingredient recommendations. Your entered targets, flavor sliders and ingredient choices are kept. Batch size and efficiency do not determine style. Choosing a style manually switches this off.
fields.Target ABV: The alcohol by volume you want, expressed as a percentage. The solver adjusts fermentable amounts and fermentation assumptions to approach it. Yeast tolerance is a limit, not a promise of that alcohol level. Optional additives such as spirits are not included in the base-beer ABV calculation.
fields.Target bitterness: The requested IBU, a calculated estimate of hop bitterness using the Tinseth formula. It is different from hop aroma and perceived bitterness. A beer can have strong dry-hop aroma with a low IBU target; dry hops add zero IBU in this model.
fields.Target color: Color is optional. Leave Set a color target off for Any color: color is excluded from numeric style matching, malt color-target ranking, and recipe scoring, including style color penalties. The resulting SRM and EBC are still predicted from fermentables using Morey. Enable it to request a specific SRM; lower values are paler and higher values darker. Color alone does not establish sweetness, roast flavor, or strength.
fields.Post-boil batch: The wort volume in the kettle after boiling, before transfer losses. Ingredient amounts and pre-boil volume are planned around this target. Expected fermenter volume is this amount minus transfer loss.
fields.Efficiency: The percentage of the malt’s potential extract recovered in the post-boil wort. Default is 72%. Lower efficiency generally needs more mash grain for the same alcohol target. Extract and sugars count at full potential in this model. Changing efficiency does not change the closest beer style.
fields.OG minimum: The lower allowed original gravity: wort density before fermentation. Water is near 1.000. Higher OG generally gives more potential alcohol, but final alcohol also depends on attenuation. Enabled gravity ranges also influence automatic style matching.
fields.OG maximum: The upper allowed original gravity. Together with the OG minimum it limits the starting wort strength the solver can choose. The range contributes to automatic style matching; it is not a measured brew result.
fields.FG minimum: The lower allowed final gravity after fermentation. FG reflects remaining extract; it helps constrain the balance between alcohol, dryness and body. The model uses yeast attenuation with approximate mash and fermentable adjustments.
fields.FG maximum: The upper allowed final gravity. A higher FG can suggest a fuller or sweeter finish, but perceived sweetness is not determined by gravity alone. The enabled range also contributes to automatic style matching.
fields.Add OG / FG constraints: Adds optional original- and final-gravity ranges alongside ABV. All these targets must work together; tight or conflicting ranges may produce tradeoffs. Turn this off to let the solver choose gravity more freely.
fields.Boil time: The total kettle boil duration in minutes. It influences evaporation planning and the maximum bittering-hop boil time. A short or zero boil can limit the bitterness that the solver can achieve.
fields.Boil-off: The expected evaporation rate per hour for your kettle. It is used to calculate the pre-boil volume needed for your post-boil batch. Enter a rate, not the total loss for this particular boil.
fields.Transfer loss: The volume left behind when moving post-boil wort to the fermenter, such as trub or kettle dead space. It must be smaller than the post-boil batch. This setting changes expected fermenter yield, not beer style.
fields.Use style flavor starting point: Replaces your flavor targets with the consensus-model estimate for a representative Recipe Book template of the current style. It is an editable sensory starting point, not official guideline prose or a measured commercial beer profile.
fields.Hop flavor direction: Loads an editable group of hop-flavor targets, such as tropical/citrus or floral/herbal. Only hop-family sliders are replaced; malt, yeast and structure preferences stay. The hop shortlist is then narrowed using matching descriptor evidence.
fields.Evaluate hop character for: Choose the addition context used to rank hops: kettle bittering, late-boil flavor, whirlpool aroma or dry hopping. The same variety can behave differently with timing. This also supplies starting doses and timings for recipe search, which can optimize them further.
fields.Hop evidence filter: Shows hops with descriptor intensity of at least 0.5/5 for at least one of your positive hop-flavor targets in the chosen usage context. It does not require every descriptor to match. Missing evidence is not proof that a flavor is absent. If no hop target is positive, the filter does not narrow the list.
fields.Flavor intensity: Your desired perceived intensity from 0 (little or none wanted) to 5 (very prominent). These sliders are subjective targets, not measurements or ingredient percentages. The consensus model estimates how a recipe may compare; it cannot guarantee the tasting result.
fields.Must include descriptor: Adds a soft sensory goal: the solver penalizes predicted intensity below 1/5 for this descriptor. It does not force a particular ingredient and is not a guaranteed flavor outcome. Ingredient availability and conflicting targets can prevent a close match.
fields.Avoid descriptor: Adds a soft sensory restriction: the solver penalizes predicted intensity above 0.3/5. This is different from excluding an ingredient, which is a hard restriction. It is not an allergy or contamination filter.
fields.Yeast form: Limits yeast candidates to dry, liquid or either form. Known alcohol tolerances below your ABV target are filtered out; unknown tolerance remains labeled for verification. Form alone does not determine flavor or the alcohol produced.
fields.Budget approach: Economy is a rough ingredient-use rule: dry yeast and no more than 4 g/L total hops. It does not use current shop prices or calculate an actual recipe cost. It may compete with high-aroma targets.
fields.On hand & excluded ingredients: An empty on-hand list permits all ingredients. Once you select any on-hand ingredients, only those selected may be used: include a suitable base malt, hops and yeast. Excluded ingredients are always forbidden. Available quantities are not tracked.
fields.flavor weight: How strongly recipe ranking favors the desired flavor profile and must/avoid descriptors. A larger value gives sensory estimates more influence relative to numeric and style penalties. The score is a ranking aid, not a measured match percentage.
fields.numbers weight: How strongly the solver favors ABV, IBU, SRM and optional gravity targets. Larger values prioritize matching those numbers relative to flavor and style. Ingredient availability and brewing limits can still prevent an exact match.
fields.style weight: How strongly the solver penalizes predictions outside the selected style’s OG, FG, ABV, IBU and SRM ranges. Automatic mode updates the selected style as you edit numeric targets. Freeform has no style penalty.
fields.Ingredient matches: A live editorial shortlist based on style-template usage, contextual descriptor evidence, numeric targets and ingredient constraints. Specs and sensory evidence are displayed separately. Choosing hops restricts the allowed pool; choosing a base malt or yeast fixes that ingredient for recipe search.
fields.Find my recipes: Searches 18 starting ingredient combinations and adjusts proportions, hop doses and process settings using deterministic brewing math and the consensus flavor model. Results are ranked starting points with tradeoffs, not guaranteed perfect matches. Open a result to edit and save it.

flavors.fruity-ester: A broad fermentation-derived fruit impression. It does not identify a specific fruit or compound; intensity and temperature response are subjective model estimates.
flavors.biscuit: Dry cracker or biscuit-like malt character.
flavors.honey: Honey-like aroma or flavor; this does not require actual honey.
flavors.dark-fruit: Dried or dark-fruit associations, such as raisin or plum.
flavors.citrus: The broad citrus-fruit family of hop associations.
flavors.tropical: The broad tropical-fruit family of hop associations.
flavors.stone-fruit: Stone-fruit associations such as peach or apricot.
flavors.spicy: Spice-like flavor associations, rather than measured chili heat.
flavors.noble: A traditional floral, herbal and spicy hop direction; this is an editorial descriptor, not a chemical measurement.
flavors.clean: A restrained fermentation profile with fewer prominent estery or phenolic associations in this model.
flavors.apple: Apple-like fruit character; a flavor target does not establish a chemical cause.
flavors.tart: A tart flavor direction; the model does not calculate acidity or pH.
flavors.funky: A broad fermentation-derived earthy or wild character; mixed-culture development is not fully modeled.
flavors.body: Perceived fullness or weight in the mouth. The model uses FG and grist proxies; body is different from alcohol strength.
flavors.sweetness: Perceived sweetness. This is a sensory estimate, not a measured sugar concentration.
flavors.bitterness: Perceived bitter intensity relative to wort strength, modeled from BU:GU. It is separate from the numeric IBU target.
flavors.dryness: A dry finishing impression, estimated from attenuation. It is not a direct moisture or sugar measurement.
flavors.carbonation: Desired carbonated mouthfeel on the 0–5 sensory scale. The solver’s carbonation setting is approximate; check the actual recipe volumes-of-CO2 setting before packaging.
flavors.astringency: A drying or puckering sensation, distinct from bitterness. This model uses a roast-grist proxy and does not calculate mash pH or tannin extraction.
